title: Construct Participation Rules
description: Registry-declared condition -> recruitment rules for condition-driven specialist/team participation (construct-pteo2, ADR-0070). A participationRules array lives alongside a registry entry (specialist, team, or a project .cx/specialists/ overlay per lib/orchestration/routing-tables.mjs's existing overlay precedent) and is resolved by the recruit stage of the pipeline ADR-0070 defines. Superset of construct-ca4's WATCHERS/evaluateWatchConditions mechanism (lib/orchestration/routing-tables.mjs): a watchCondition names a boolean predicate over requestSignals and is one valid form of `when`; this schema additionally carries role, gate, and enforcement scope, which ca4's mechanism has no field for. Enforcement (gate: enforced) is never implied by this schema alone — it is only realized when the recruiting team's own registry entry (schemas/scope.schema.json's team.decisionRights) names the same decisionRight in enforcementScope.decisionRight, per ADR-0070's opt-in-per-team decision.

participationRule.description: One when(signals) -> recruit(specialists|teams) rule. `id` must be unique within the owning registry entry's rules array; duplicate ids across entries are a registry-assembly error, matching the existing duplicate-ownership check for events/docs in lib/orchestration/routing-tables.mjs.

id.description: Stable identifier for this rule, referenced in trace/telemetry output and by decisionRights bindings.

dimension.description: Optional classification of what concern this rule recruits for. `legal-compliance` is a first-class dimension (ADR-0070) bound structurally to cx-security via the legalComplianceBinding conditional below — it is not a 13th role.

role.description: The recruited participant's function on the artifact this run produces. Fixed 3-value enum — adding a role here is an ADR-0070 amendment, not a per-rule choice.

gate.description: advisory: recruitment and sign-off are recorded but never block the run. enforced: a missing sign-off from this rule's recruited participant blocks release. Default is advisory (ADR-0070, binding user decision) — enforced requires enforcementScope naming a decisionRight the recruiting team's own registry entry (schemas/scope.schema.json team.decisionRights) actually declares; the schema-level if/then below makes this a structural requirement, not prose.

enforcementScope.description: Required when gate=enforced. Names the exact team + decisionRight whose registry entry must list decisionRight in its decisionRights array (schemas/scope.schema.json) for this rule's enforcement to take effect — enforcement is opt-in per team, never global.

reason.description: Human-readable justification surfaced in trace output, matching watcherToReason in lib/orchestration/routing-tables.mjs.

allOf.$comment: Structural enforcement of the no-13th-role decision (ADR-0070): a rule whose dimension is legal-compliance must recruit cx-security as one of its specialists. This is checked here, not left to prose, so a rule that invents a standalone legal/compliance recruit target fails schema validation.

dimension.description: Concern the rule recruits for. Not a role — a dimension is bound to an existing roster role (e.g. legal-compliance -> cx-security); it never introduces a new specialist type.

whenCondition.description: The condition side of when(signals) -> recruit(...). `watchCondition` names a predicate already registered in lib/orchestration/routing-tables.mjs's WATCHERS map (the ca4 mechanism this schema supersedes); `signalExpr` is the ADR-0070 generalization for a signal not yet named as a watchCondition. At least one of the two is required so every rule is traceable to a concrete evaluable condition.

watchCondition.description: Name of a predicate over requestSignals, e.g. one of ca4's 5 shipped watchers (lib/orchestration/routing-tables.mjs:29-39: high-ambiguity-deep-work, visual-or-ui-risk, auth-payments-non-narrow, architecture-without-metric, wide-blast-radius) or a signal added under construct-pteo2.3's externalized signal set.

signalExpr.description: A boolean expression over the requestSignals shape (lib/orchestration-policy.mjs), evaluated the same way WATCHERS predicates are today. Free-form now; construct-pteo2.3 is scoped to define the expression grammar and the full externalized signal vocabulary this references.

recruitTarget.description: What gets pulled onto the field when `when` is true. At least one of specialists/teams is required.

rosterSpecialist.description: Fixed 12-role roster (specialists/org/specialists/*.json). A rule can only recruit an existing role — this schema has no mechanism for declaring a 13th, per this repo's CLAUDE.md invariant that a profile selects flows + skill emphasis over the fixed roster and does not invent new roles or departments.
